list.heading: Memory
list.description: The memory items the connected Core reports, scoped exactly as the Core reports them. The list is served and paginated by the Core; this surface shows only what the Core returns and invents no items, counts, or totals. Pending review is a lifecycle state, never a trust claim; memory stays separate from canonical knowledge truth.
list.emptyAllBody: The Core reports no memory items for this view. Nothing is invented here: an item appears only from the Core's own confirmed state, through the Add item action or the Core's own extraction path when one exists.
list.emptyPendingBody: The Core reports no items in its pending-review state for this view. Pending review is a lifecycle state, never a trust claim; approval is an explicit user action whose confirmation only the Core's response carries.
list.failureTitle: The memory list could not be read
list.failureBody: The Core returned a typed refusal for this read. The stable code below is the machine identifier; no memory content is included in it.
list.unknownTitle: The memory list response was lost
list.unknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for this read. This is never proof that the list is empty or unchanged — the truthful unknown state is shown until a fresh read confirms.
list.connectionHint: Check the Core connection and try again.

add.title: Add a memory item
add.scopeNote: The scope is stated at creation and carried on every read; it never silently broadens afterward.
add.refsNote: One reference per line. The source event is shown, never rewritten; the Core preserves provenance on every later edit.
add.originValue: A user-created item is user-entered. The Core validates the origin claim: model-extracted origin can only be set by the Core's own extraction path, and no client body claims it — so this form offers no origin choice.
add.secretsValue: Passwords, API keys, private keys, and payment credentials are never stored in Memory. A write attempting secret storage is refused by the Core (MEMORY_SECRETS_REJECTED) and the matched material is never displayed. A secret-manager reference may be stored instead.
add.confirmedEntryStateNote: The response's lifecycle_state carries the Core-confirmed entry state — never an assumption. A user-entered add is not model-extracted content; pending review is reserved for the Core's own extraction path.
add.unknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for the add. This is never proof of success or failure. The correlation ID for this add was {{correlationId}}.
add.unknownReconcileNote: Reconcile before any retry: re-issuing with the SAME key and the SAME request identity is the Core's replay ruling — it returns the recorded item without creating a duplicate; the list re-reads from the Core's confirmed state when this dialog closes.

detail.heading: Memory item
detail.identityHeading: Identity and state (as the Core reports it)
detail.failureTitle: This memory item could not be read
detail.unknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for this read. This is never proof that the item is gone or unchanged — the truthful unknown state is shown until a fresh read confirms.
detail.secretsLawNote: Secrets are never stored in Memory: password, API-key, private-key, and payment-credential values are refused by the Core — only secret-manager references may be stored, and no secret value is ever displayed here.
detail.provenanceNote: The source event is shown, never rewritten; provenance is never silently rewritten by an edit, and the origin label is preserved on every correction.
detail.conflictHeading: Conflict / freshness (as the Core reports it)
detail.reviewDisabledReason: The Core serves approve and reject for items in its pending-review state. No pending-review item is producible through the public API (no extraction producer exists on this surface), so no item is currently reviewable here — these controls stay disabled with that reason, and the Core's typed review-state refusal (MEMORY_REVIEW_STATE_CONFLICT) governs any direct attempt.
detail.reviewDistinctNote: Pending review is a lifecycle state, never a trust claim. Approval is an explicit user action: model-extracted content never becomes user-confirmed without it, and only the Core's confirmed response carries the outcome.
detail.pinFailureTitle: The Core refused the pin change
detail.pinUnknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for the pin change. This is never proof that the pin state changed or stayed the same.
detail.pinUnknownNote: Reconcile before a repeat: re-read the item's authoritative state first — a repeat without reconciliation can double-apply.

edit.title: Edit this memory item
edit.preservesValue: The edit creates the Core-defined revision/update event: the origin label is preserved, the originating references are never silently rewritten, and the edit alone never constitutes review approval.
edit.secretsValue: The corrected content is subject to the same law: secrets are never stored in Memory; a corrected body attempting secret storage is refused by the Core (MEMORY_SECRETS_REJECTED).
edit.unknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for the edit. This is never proof of success or failure. The correlation ID for this edit was {{correlationId}}.
edit.unknownReconcileNote: Reconcile before any retry: the item's authoritative read resolves the edit's outcome by the item identity — then a new, explicit edit (with a fresh identity) can follow.

destructive.scopeStatement: The Core will apply this action to the item's active store entry; derived references, sync state, and backup retention follow the Core's retention policy exactly as it defines them.
destructive.retentionStance: Immediate erasure of every replica or backup is never promised by this surface — the Core-confirmed outcome carries the retention caveat, which renders exactly as the Core returns it (empty means none reported).
destructive.openDistinctnessNote: Whether Forget and Delete name distinct Core semantics is Core-defined and open: this surface renders each member exactly as the Core serves it and never asserts more than the confirmed outcome delivers. Memory deletion never auto-deletes KnowledgePack claims.
destructive.retentionNote: Retention caveat (as the Core returns it)
destructive.unknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for this action. This is NEVER assumed to have applied: the outcome is unknown until reconciled. The correlation ID for this action was {{correlationId}}.
destructive.unknownReconcileNote: Reconcile before any retry: re-issuing with the SAME key and the SAME request identity is the Core's replay ruling — it returns the recorded outcome without applying again.

inclusion.title: Per-request inclusion
inclusion.requestRefNote: The stated request/scope reference this decision applies to — the ONLY scope it applies to. It never widens the item's scope and never changes another scope.
inclusion.scopeNote: This is a per-request decision, not an item-state change: it changes no lifecycle state and has no global effect. Retention is request-lifetime at most.
inclusion.confirmedNote: This is a decision record, not an item state: the item's lifecycle state is unchanged, and the decision applies only to the stated request.

export.title: Export memory items
export.scopeNote: The exact export scope is shown before generation, never assumed. An item-scoped export names exactly those items and the item's own scope — scope never silently broadens.
export.destinationNote: A descriptive label for where this export is going — displayed before generation, never assumed by the Core.
export.secretsValue: This is a prohibition, not a preference: no secret value ever enters an export artifact (the binding secrets law extends to exports). The stored items carry no secret values — the law refused them at write time.
export.submitFailureBody: The typed refusal below is the Core's own answer; the stable code is the machine identifier.
export.truncatedTrue: Yes — the range exceeded the finite bound
export.truncatedNote: The truncation flag is the Core's own honest statement — a range exceeding the finite bound truncates honestly, never silently.
export.exportRefNote: The export reference is a content digest — a content identity, never a truth, safety, or authenticity claim.
export.noDownloadNote: The served family carries no artifact download route; the export document rode this response body. No download surface is invented here.
export.unknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for the export. This is never proof of success or failure. The correlation ID for this export was {{correlationId}}.
export.unknownReissueNote: The export reads and mutates nothing; each re-issue creates a new export operation (the coded retry class is safe-retry). The re-issue is an explicit action — never an auto-retry.

failure.MEMORY_SCOPE_VIOLATION: The read or export crossed the stated scope. Scope never silently broadens — the stated scope governs every operation.
failure.MEMORY_SECRETS_REJECTED: The Core refused this content: secrets (passwords, API keys, private keys, payment credentials) are never stored in Memory. A secret-manager reference may be stored instead. The matched material is never displayed.
failure.MEMORY_ITEM_NOT_FOUND: The Core reports no such item. Unknown and out-of-scope items carry the same typed response — no existence is inferred from it.
failure.MEMORY_REVIEW_STATE_CONFLICT: The Core reports this item is not in its required review state: approve and reject apply only to items in the Core's pending-review state.
failure.MEMORY_CONFLICT: A concurrent edit was detected: the prepared-against state no longer matches. Re-read the item's authoritative state — never overwrite.
failure.MEMORY_NOT_EDITABLE: The Core reports this item as not editable. Eligibility is the Core's own decision, never the UI's.
failure.CONFLICT_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: The same idempotency key was presented with a different request identity. A new, explicit action with a fresh key is the path forward.
failure.CONFLICT_STATE: The recorded state conflicts with this request (for example, a replay past its window). A new, explicit action is the path forward.
failure.NOT_FOUND: The Core reports no such operation record.
failure.AUTHZ_DENIED: The Core's authorization boundary refused this action.
failure.INTERNAL: The Core reported an internal error.
failure.unknown: The Core returned an unrecognized code: it is shown verbatim as the stable language-neutral identifier it is.
failure.recoveryReconcileItem: Re-read the item's authoritative state before any retry — never overwrite.
failure.recoveryNotFound: Return to the list and re-read from the Core's confirmed state.
failure.recoveryFixInput: Fix the request (scope, content, or identity) and issue a new, explicit action.
failure.recoveryAuthz: Check the session and try again from a connected surface.
failure.recoveryRetry: Retry as an explicit action once the connection recovers.
failure.recoveryUnknown: Retry as an explicit user action; reconcile through the authoritative reads before any repeat.
